unit.why: A tale about the Shelah (R. Isaiah Horowitz, pre-Hasidic) and his student who became a robber chief and repented; it is framed as told by the Hasidic master of Neskhiz.

stories.start_quote: מרן מנסכיז היה מפליא מאד לימוד
stories.end_quote: ע״י תשובה זו נעשה צדיק גמור
stories.summary_en: The Shelah's student is struck by his master and runs away to become a robber chief. The Shelah later strays into his forest hideout, and the student threatens to kill him unless he gives him a penance. The Shelah prescribes a snake to be fed for seven years until it kills him, and through this the student becomes a perfect tzaddik.

tags.why: Praises the Shelah, a pre-Hasidic authority.
